cards.q: What does EIGRP authentication do?
cards.a: EIGRP authentication lets a router verify that received EIGRP packets were generated by a neighbor possessing the configured key, protecting the adjacency from unauthorized or misconfigured peers. It is configured per interface / address-family interface (not per area), can use MD5 or HMAC-SHA-256, and is not enabled by default.

cards.q: Which EIGRP authentication methods exist?
cards.a: None (default, authentication disabled), MD5 (legacy message authentication common in classic EIGRP), and HMAC-SHA-256 (stronger cryptographic authentication supported by modern named-mode implementations). Focus on MD5, HMAC-SHA-256, and key chains for CCNP/ENCOR; EIGRP plaintext authentication is not the normal method.

cards.q: What does EIGRP authentication actually protect?
cards.a: It verifies the integrity and authenticity of EIGRP packets and prevents unauthorized devices from participating in the EIGRP adjacency. It provides packet authentication and integrity, not confidentiality, so it does not encrypt the routing information.

cards.q: How are key chains structured and how does EIGRP identify keys?
cards.a: key chain EIGRP-KEYS contains one or more keys, each with a key-string such as SecretKey123 and a key ID. The key ID lets EIGRP identify which configured key is being used.

cards.q: What are send-lifetime and accept-lifetime in an EIGRP key chain?
cards.a: Send-lifetime controls when the router can use the key for outgoing authenticated packets. Accept-lifetime controls when the router accepts packets authenticated with that key.

cards.q: How should key rotation be designed to avoid an authentication gap?
cards.a: Configure multiple keys so credentials can be changed without an outage. Ensure the old and new keys have an appropriate overlap period so one side never sends with a key the other side is no longer accepting, and no packets are rejected during the transition.

cards.q: What commands configure classic IPv4 EIGRP authentication?
cards.a: Create the key chain, then on the interface run ip authentication mode eigrp <AS> md5 and ip authentication key-chain eigrp <AS> <KEY-CHAIN>. Authentication must be configured consistently on the interfaces forming the adjacency.

cards.q: Where is authentication configured in named EIGRP?
cards.a: Under router eigrp <name> → address-family → af-interface <interface> with authentication mode (for example hmac-sha-256) and authentication key-chain EIGRP-KEYS.

cards.q: How do you apply the same EIGRP authentication to all interfaces of an address family?
cards.a: Use af-interface default under the named EIGRP address family, for example authentication mode hmac-sha-256 and authentication key-chain EIGRP-KEYS under af-interface default.

cards.q: Is HMAC-SHA-256 automatically enabled in named EIGRP?
cards.a: No. HMAC-SHA-256 provides stronger authentication than MD5, but it is not automatic. You must configure authentication mode hmac-sha-256 and associate a key chain that sets cryptographic-algorithm hmac-sha-256.

cards.q: What happens if authentication parameters do not match between two EIGRP neighbors?
cards.a: The EIGRP adjacency will fail to establish or remain operational. Both neighbors must use compatible authentication configuration, including matching algorithm, key, and key chain.

cards.q: Is EIGRP authentication an area-wide concept like OSPF?
cards.a: No. EIGRP has no OSPF-style area-wide authentication model. Authentication is associated with each EIGRP interface or address-family interface, so authentication can differ between interfaces if the design requires it.

cards.q: How does authentication apply to EIGRP for IPv6?
cards.a: The concepts are the same. In named mode, configure under the IPv6 address family af-interface, for example authentication mode hmac-sha-256 and authentication key-chain EIGRP-KEYS. Both EIGRP neighbors must use compatible authentication configuration.

cards.q: What is the difference between authentication and encryption?
cards.a: Authentication answers 'Did this packet come from a peer that knows the secret, and has it been altered?' providing integrity and authenticity. Encryption answers 'Can someone else read the packet contents?' providing confidentiality. EIGRP authentication does not encrypt EIGRP routing updates.

cards.q: Is configuring a key chain the same as enabling EIGRP authentication?
cards.a: No. A key chain stores the authentication keys; EIGRP must also be configured to use the key chain via authentication mode and authentication key-chain under the AF interface. Defining the key chain alone does not authenticate anything.

cards.q: When an EIGRP neighbor does not appear, what do you check for authentication?
cards.a: Use show ip eigrp neighbors, then show ip eigrp interfaces detail. Verify authentication mode, key chain, key string, algorithm, key lifetime, EIGRP AS, and interface configuration.

cards.q: What causes EIGRP authentication failure?
cards.a: Wrong key string, wrong key ID, wrong algorithm, wrong key chain, an expired key, send/accept lifetime mismatch, or authentication configured on only one side.

cards.q: What should you check when a key change causes EIGRP adjacency flaps?
cards.a: Check show key chain for the current active key, send-lifetime, accept-lifetime, expired keys, and missing overlap. A lifetime gap can cause packets to be rejected during the transition.

cards.q: Which commands verify EIGRP authentication configuration?
cards.a: show key chain displays configured key chains and key/lifetime information. show ip eigrp interfaces detail checks interface configuration and authentication details. show ip eigrp neighbors shows whether the expected neighbor appears. show running-config | section key chain and show running-config | section router eigrp verify the actual configuration.

cards.q: What does a neighbor disappearing after a key change, or authentication working on one link but not another, indicate?
cards.a: A neighbor disappearing after a key change indicates a key lifetime problem, so check show key chain. Authentication working on one link but not another indicates a per-interface configuration difference, so check each address-family interface.

cards.q: What is the core formula for EIGRP authentication?
cards.a: EIGRP Authentication = Key Chain + Authentication Algorithm + EIGRP Interface/AF Configuration + Matching Parameters on Both Neighbors.
